notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0004] Mirror existing error codes and validation order from sibling functions: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and state-check-first pattern rather than inventing new ones.
  Before implementing a new function, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same message format and check ordering used by analogous functions like issue_invoice/authorize. This keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on error codes.
- [rb-0002] Inspect existing module conventions before implementing: Reading sibling functions in the target file reveals required helpers and patterns like to_money, ZERO, and round_money.
  Before writing a new function, read the surrounding module (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to see how money is normalized and rounded. Mirror those conventions so the new function is consistent and passes hidden tests.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty collections with the project's zero constant: For aggregate functions over possibly-empty lists, return the module's ZERO constant rather than a literal 0 or Decimal(0).
  Guard against division by zero by checking total quantity first and returning ZERO. Use sum(..., ZERO) as the start value so the accumulator stays a Decimal and matches project style.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money via round_money before range checks: Convert unit_price with the project's round_money helper, then compare against ZERO, so string/float inputs and rounding are handled uniformly.
  Accept flexible price inputs by calling round_money(unit_price) first, then validate `price < ZERO` and store the rounded Decimal on the LineItem. This matches how line_total and authorize handle amounts and avoids type errors on raw strings/floats.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer inputs in Python: isinstance(True, int) is True, so explicitly reject bools before the int check.
  When a parameter must be a positive integer, write `if isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0: raise ...` — otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and hidden tests for invalid quantity will fail.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any validation or mutation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result early, before state checks or side effects.
item.content: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` on every balance-changing operation. Scan `audit.events(<event_name>)` for a matching key and return the original record immediately; only then validate state and apply changes. Always include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Enforce approval thresholds as optional keyword-only params
item.description: Amounts above a policy threshold need a second approver; accept `approved_by=None` so existing callers keep working and raise BillingError when missing.
item.content: For refunds/credits above 500.00 (finance policy FIN-2026-03), raise `BillingError("approval_required")` if `approved_by` is None; amounts at or below the threshold need no approval. Keep the threshold as a module constant and record `approved_by` in the audit entry.

item.title: Mirror sibling module patterns for errors, money, and audit
item.description: Before writing a new function, read adjacent modules (payments.py, money.py, errors.py, audit.py) and reuse their helpers and error codes for consistency.
item.content: Use `round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, and `BillingError(code, detail)` with codes like `invalid_state`, `non_positive_amount`. Validate state (e.g. status must be 'captured'), reject non-positive amounts, and cap cumulative refunds at the captured amount before mutating `refunded_amount`/`status`.
